properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Vendored crypto-js bundle inside web3.js, embedded in geth's JSRE (console) runtime. RC4 is registered on the CryptoJS surface and invokable from any console script; no application call site in the Go code. Algorithm ships with the binary.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Same vendored crypto-js bundle (inside web3.js) shipping TripleDES (64-bit block, Sweet32) alongside RC4; available to JSRE console scripts, unused by geth's Go code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Posture control in the Engine API auth path: library claims validation is off by design (clock-drift tolerance between CL and EL), with equivalent manual checks (expiry, iat presence, ±60s freshness) enforced in the same function. No verification gap remains; do not treat as a disabled-signature vulnerability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js HmacMD5 registered in the vendored web3.js bundle; invokable from geth JSRE console scripts; no Go-side call site.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum's core signing curve — ECDSA over secp256k1 via crypto/crypto.go and the vendored libsecp256k1 C library (which this tree builds with the ecdh/ellswift/extrakeys modules). Used for account keys, transaction signatures, ENR node records and the devp2p identity scheme. Shor-vulnerable signature primitive; replacement is ML-DSA-65/SLH-DSA in principle, but in practice migration is a chain-level (EIP) decision, not fixable per call site here. Changeable here only jointly with the protocol.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Posture class: digest comparisons with == across consensus and codec code. The two genuinely secret-keyed MAC comparisons in this repo live in the scwallet secure channel (bytes.Equal at accounts/scwallet/securechannel.go:104/256) and are NOT part of this operator-based site set — reported as a separate finding. For contrast, the RLPx frame/header MACs ARE constant-time (hmac.Equal at p2p/rlpx/rlpx.go:173/198), so the p2p transport does not share this weakness.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Unauthenticated stream modes in this tree are always paired with a MAC: keystore v3 = AES-128-CTR + keccak-256 MAC; ECIES = AES-CTR + HMAC-SHA-2 tag (constant-time compare); RLPx = AES-CTR + keccak MAC; discv5 = AES-CTR for masking within its AEAD-framed protocol. So the CTR/CBC "malleable" concern is mitigated by encrypt-then-MAC at every site. Quantum posture: Grover-only on the AES-128 keys (64-bit margin).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-CBC in geth's accounts code: (1) presale-wallet import — key from PBKDF2-SHA256 with only 2000 iterations, CBC without a MAC, mitigated only by the address-consistency check — a legacy-format compatibility path, weak by modern standards but fixed by the historical pyethsaletool format; (2) the keycard/scwallet secure channel uses CBC paired with a separate MAC (encrypt-then-MAC pattern). Quantum posture: symmetric, Grover-only; AES-128 retains 64-bit quantum margin.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA keygen on secp256k1: accounts/keystore/key.go (new keystore keys), crypto/crypto.go (node/account key generation), crypto/ecies (ECIES ephemeral keys), crypto/secp256k1 test. Not FIPS-DSA — same logical asset as the secp256k1 object ALG-673c8f24, reached by the "dsa-usage" rule name.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js HmacSHA1 registered in the vendored web3.js bundle; available to JSRE console scripts; no Go-side call site. SHA-1 usage would still be a weak-hash finding for any console script that adopts it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Engine API (authrpc.JWTSecret) authentication between consensus and execution client, per the Ethereum execution-apis spec: 32-byte shared secret, HS256 only. The secret file is also generated by geth when absent (node/config). HMAC-SHA256 key recovery is quantum-weakened (Grover) but 256-bit HMAC remains above 128-bit quantum security; the PQ path for this protocol would be an ML-DSA/EdDSA-signed token scheme, not yet standardized for the Engine API.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA (secp256k1 via crypto.S256()) is the account, node-identity, and discovery-signature algorithm of this codebase: keystore account keys (accounts/keystore/key.go GenerateKey op-chains), devp2p node identity (p2p/config + config_toml PrivateKey fields, enode ENR/URL v4 scheme, RLPx handshake dialDest/remote pubkeys, discv4 packet verification), abigen transactor keys, ethkey CLI keygen. Shor-broken; the EVM's own secp256k1 recovery is tracked separately under the secp256k1 object (scout 1).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH over secp256k1 in geth's P2P stack: RLPx transport handshake (GenerateShared + keccak KDF → AES-CTR + keccak MAC session keys) and discv5 handshake (eph := ecdh(priv, pub) → HKDF/AES-GCM session). Both are classical ephemeral agreements; a recorded handshake is decryptable once Shor-capable hardware exists. The libsecp256k1 bench sites record the vendored ECDH/ellswift module capability (no application call site uses the module directly; ecies computes its agreement in Go).

components.name: Go crypto/tls sessions on default settings (Go 1.25.0)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Positive control worth recording: ECIES decryption compares its HMAC tag in constant time. Contrast with the keystore MAC check (accounts/keystore/passphrase.go) which uses bytes.Equal — that side is inventoried separately in the non-constant-time-comparison object.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECIES supports NIST P-384/P-521 in addition to secp256k1: the params registry (crypto/ecies/params.go) maps them to AES-192-SHA384/AES-256-SHA512 parameter sets, tested in ecies_test.go. Classical Shor-vulnerable curves; in practice geth callers use the package with secp256k1, but the capability is compiled and exported here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Keccak-256 (the pre-NIST-padding SHA-3 variant) is Ethereum's universal hash: RLP/tx/block hashing, address derivation, the keystore MAC (accounts/keystore/passphrase.go), the RLPx wire MAC (p2p/rlpx) and the ethash cache/dataset seeding. Grover-only exposure (256→128-bit quantum security); it is the tree's data-integrity backbone and any address-based signature migration depends on it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 is a workhorse here: EIP-4844 versioned blob hashes (sha256 over KZG commitment), beacon-chain Merkleization, PBKDF2 as the PRF, block-header SSZ hashing, clef attestation of JS rules, filtermaps log indexing. Grover-only (128-bit quantum security at 256-bit output).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 for password-based key derivation: keystore v3 (user-set, standard vectors use ≥10240 and light 4096 scrypt-equivalents), keycard pairing (50000), and the presale import at 2000 iterations — that one is below any modern minimum but is dictated by the historical pyethsaletool format for reading old wallets; it decrypts user-supplied files rather than protecting newly written data.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: First-party BLAKE2b: geth ships its own crypto/blake2b implementation (including the BLAKE2X XOF wrapper), registers BLAKE2b-256/384/512 in the Go hash registry, and drives the F compression function for EIP-152 (F precompile). Symmetric, Grover-only; BLAKE2b-512 keeps 256-bit quantum security, the 256-bit variant 128-bit. Also present transitively: lukechampine.com/blake3 (indirect dep).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES block cipher as instantiated throughout accounts and p2p crypto: keystore v3 (AES-128-CTR), presale import (AES-128-CBC), keycard channel (AES-128-CBC+MAC), ECIES symmetric layer (AES-128/192/256-CTR per curve params), RLPx transport (AES-CTR) and discv5 (AES-GCM via the separate AES-GCM object). Grover halves key strength: AES-128 → 64-bit quantum margin (the dominant instantiation here); CNSA 2.0 target would be AES-256.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-128 is the keystore format standard (Web3 Secret Storage v3: scrypt/PBKDF2 → AES-128-CTR + keccak-256 MAC) and the presale/keycard channel cipher. Format-compatibility constraints mean the key size is not unilaterally changeable (interop with every Ethereum keystore consumer); CNSA 2.0 would want AES-256, Grover leaves 64-bit quantum margin here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt (golang.org/x/crypto/scrypt) is the default keystore v3 password KDF (memory-hard; standard params N=262144,r=8,p=1). Quantum posture: Grover halves to ~2^17 memory-hard work — scrypt's cost model degrades less than PBKDF2's, but both remain password-strength-bound. Parameters are recorded per-file in every keystore JSON.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AEAD layer of two live systems: (1) discv5 node-discovery protocol — AES-GCM with a 16-byte session key (AES-128 floor) from HKDF-SHA256 over secp256k1 ECDH, 12-byte nonces via NewGCMWithNonceSize, Seal/Open of v5wire packets; (2) clef's AESEncryptedStorage — aes.NewCipher on the caller-supplied key + cipher.NewGCM + Seal/Open with crypto/rand nonce and the KV key as AAD (anti-entry-swap binding). AES-GCM is quantum-acceptable (Grover halves the discv5 key to ~64-bit, the weakest point in the re

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HMAC-SHA-2 family: BIP-32 master-key MAC in accounts/scwallet, plus the crypto-js HMAC surface bundled into the geth console's web3.js (used by console JS for its sha3/HMAC helpers). Quantum-safe against Grover at 256+ bits for the SHA-512 variant.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: HKDF-SHA256 (golang.org/x/crypto/hkdf) derives the discv5 packet-key schedule from the ephemeral secp256k1 ECDH output. The KDF itself is Grover-only; the ECDH feeding it is the Shor-vulnerable part (cross-reference: ECDH object ALG-c9ffc8a8).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECIES's KDF: turns the secp256k1 ECDH shared secret into encryption+MAC keys using SHA-256/384/512 per the curve's parameter set. Symmetric KDF — Grover-only; the quantum risk lives in the ECDH below it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared (indirect) dependency of the cmd/keeper module (Ziren zkvm keeper tool): golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 at cmd/keeper/go.mod:82 pulls the sha3/Keccak implementation into that module's build graph; keeper code does not import it directly. Dependency inventory entry — presence is the recorded fact.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHAKE128 (128-bit extensible-output function) available via x/crypto/sha3 in the cmd/keeper module graph (golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 indirect, cmd/keeper/go.mod:82). Under Grover its 128-bit security halves to ~64-bit; any future keeper use for key material should prefer SHAKE256.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-384/SHA-512 usage: BIP-32/44 hierarchical wallet derivation for the keycard account path, the scwallet pairing channel, and as the ECIES hash parameter for the NIST-curve parameter sets. Grover-only exposure; SHA-384/512 retain ≥192-bit quantum security.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHAKE256 XOF available via x/crypto/sha3 in the cmd/keeper module graph (golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 indirect, cmd/keeper/go.mod:82); 256-bit output keeps ~128-bit quantum security — acceptable posture if adopted.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Go crypto/rand CSPRNG supplies keystore salt/IV, scwallet pairing secrets, ECIES ephemeral keys and RLPx/discv5 handshake nonces. Quantum-irrelevant (no Shor/Grover concern for a CSPRNG itself); recorded as the RNG backbone of the key-management paths. The math/rand uses inventoried separately (non-cryptographic PRNG object) are in non-key paths.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Engine-API authentication (EIP-3631-style): the execution client signs/verifies auth JWTs with HS256 (HMAC-SHA256) using the shared --authrpc.jwtsecret. HMAC-SHA256 is Grover-only; the notable posture items are the HS256 (symmetric) choice and the jwt_handler options — see the JWT-verification-disabled and JWT-HS256 objects. Changeable here (a config/algorithm choice, not a protocol constraint).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Primary extended-crypto provider for the application layer: x/crypto supplies scrypt/pbkdf2 (keystore KDFs), hkdf (discv5 key schedule) and sha3. Version v0.53.0 is recent; no post-quantum algorithms are consumed from it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Protocol-tier record of the DTLS capability shipped in the dependency graph (libp2p WebRTC transport for the cometbft stack). Harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to DTLS-session traffic; no first-party call site configures its groups.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: WebRTC data/media channel protection (libp2p WebRTC transport in the cometbft dependency chain): DTLS-SRTP with classical key agreement. Observable here; changeable only through dependency upgrades upstream.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The Go extended-cryptography provider (golang.org/x/crypto: curves, KDFs, ciphers, SSH) declared as an indirect dependency of cmd/keeper at go.mod:82 — this is the module-level provider record; the scrypt/pbkdf2/hkdf/sha3/openpgp sub-package objects below are its facets. The keeper module pulls it via the Ziren zkvm runtime and geth; the version (v0.53.0) is what decides the module's PQ capability going forward.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: OpenPGP surface shipped by the deprecated golang.org/x/crypto/openpgp package, carried into the cmd/keeper module graph by golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 (cmd/keeper/go.mod:82). The package is frozen/unmaintained upstream; no direct import found in keeper code. Recorded as dependency inventory; do not build new features on it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: QUIC transport available in the shipped dependency graph (libp2p QUIC transport for the cometbft stack). All its key exchanges are classical; recorded traffic would be decryptable under Shor. No first-party configuration of its TLS groups exists.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: DNSSEC capability in the dependency graph (libp2p/DNS peer discovery). No first-party call site performs DNSSEC validation explicitly; capability is compiled in and reachable via the dependency's own API.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Committed geth test private key (secp256k1, 256-bit) consumed by cmd/geth account tests; a long-standing public fixture whose address is baked into test expectations. Not production material, but it is key material in the repo — changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared (indirect) dependency of cmd/keeper: golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 (go.mod:82) ships the scrypt KDF. Memory-hard PBKDF for password-derived keys; no direct scrypt import found in keeper source, but the module builds it into the graph.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Maintained JWT library (v4.5.2); provides HS256 signing for the engine API. Same logical dependency as the JWT-signing algorithm object; kept as the provider entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: QUIC transport crypto available via the consensus-layer dependency stack (cometbft/libp2p): TLS 1.3 handshake with classical (X25519/ECDHE) key exchange — harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to any QUIC traffic it carries. Observable here, replaceable only by upstream dependency upgrades; no geth call site configures its cipher suites.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Deprecated JWT library in the build graph as a transitive dependency — a supply-chain hygiene finding: it should be audited out (identify the requiring module and upgrade it to golang-jwt). No first-party import of dgrijalva/jwt-go exists in this tree; risk is latent (any dependency that does import it inherits the vulnerable parsing).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: DTLS provider in the dependency graph via libp2p's WebRTC transport (cometbft stack). Classical key agreement only; observable here, changeable only via dependency upgrades. The ALG-166cbbb4 object records the same capability at the protocol tier.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared (indirect) dependency of cmd/keeper: golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 (go.mod:82) ships the pbkdf2 KDF. Any keeper use for key derivation should carry OWASP-level iteration counts (the root module's accounts/keystore uses 262144 for v3 keystores — same package family).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared (indirect) dependency of cmd/keeper: golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 (go.mod:82) ships the HKDF key-derivation function — the same KDF the root module uses for discv5 session keys (p2p/discover/v5wire/crypto.go).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Declared (indirect) dependency of cmd/keeper: golang.org/x/crypto v0.53.0 (go.mod:82) ships the deprecated, unmaintained openpgp package. No direct import in keeper source; recorded because the module graph carries the code, and OpenPGP's RSA/ElGamal surface is quantum-broken if ever invoked.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Dependency-inventory record for x/crypto/sha3 (SHA-3/Keccak) in the cmd/keeper module graph — same declared package as the algorithm-view object ALG-c9ef78a4; referenced there for the algorithm semantics.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: WebRTC stack (pion) in the dependency graph via cometbft/libp2p; its SRTP media/data channel security is DTLS-SRTP (classical ECDHE key agreement → AES AEAD). Same stack as the DTLS and DTLS-SRTP algorithm objects.

properties.name: pqs:context
